entries.test: Public evaluations and incident investigations can establish whether unusual situations frequently confound machine-learning systems and cause driverless-car failures.
entries.note: The source identifies edge cases as a problem; the proposition adds the ranking 'main problem'.

entries.test: Public technical demonstrations and operational records available by August 2023 can show whether any driverless-car system had solved general handling of unanticipated road situations.
entries.note: Not having figured out how to build something differs from not having built it.
The persistence of edge cases is factual. The central assessment of 'too much' data and 'not enough' reasoning supplies no objective standard for the appropriate balance.
The aside invites an analogy with LLMs without specifying exactly which preceding claims carry over. The proposition turns that suggestion into a definite technical assessment.

entries.test: Public operating protocols and deployment records can establish whether every self-driving vehicle on public roads in August 2023 had an onboard safety driver or remote human assistance.
entries.note: Marcus endorses the factual explanation attributed to Metz. That explanation concerns vehicles on public roads; the proposition extends its universal oversight claim beyond that scope.

entries.test: Public incident reports, traffic records and fleet operating records can establish whether expanded San Francisco operations caused the described stalls and traffic disruptions.
entries.note: 'Has led' asserts causation. The surrounding examples give 'chaos' a concrete reading as operational failures and traffic disruption.

entries.test: Public documentation of training coverage and novel road incidents can establish whether increasing training data continues to leave driverless cars encountering previously uncovered situations.
entries.note: This is a general claim about the limits of training coverage, illustrated by existing incidents.
The central claim condemns the expansion as reckless. Accidents can inform that judgment but cannot settle whether the decision was 'insane'.

entries.test: Public reports of humanoid-robot deployments can establish whether deployed robots encounter numerous unusual situations, alongside documented edge cases in driving and medicine.
entries.note: The robot prediction expressly depends on deployment. The proposition omits that qualification and weakens the prediction of numerous edge cases to their mere presence.
He frames the recommendation as a rhetorical question, which the supplied endorsement rule excludes. Its substance is a conditional recommendation about research priorities.
The source says 'likely' and 'probably'. Its antecedent is failing to shift research focus, whereas the proposition substitutes failing to develop new methods.
The source expresses Marcus's personal assessment of deserved trust. The proposition turns that into an objective qualification for operating without human involvement.
